# Reasoning as the farmer

Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming these 8 mu for fifty years — I was born on this land and I'll probably die on it. My wife and I are the only two left in the household now; the children are in Handan and Shijiazhuang, they send money and come back at wheat harvest and cotton picking, but I can't count on them for the daily work. At 76 my back isn't what it used to be, so I have to be careful about how much labor I take on.

I finished senior high and I've been to a lot of extension trainings over the years, so I pay attention to the numbers — N rates, planting density, irrigation timing. But book knowledge only gets you so far on this soil. I know my fields: the west plot is sandier, the east plot holds water better. That's experience, not a soil test.

Here's how I'm splitting the 8 mu this year:

- **6 mu wheat-maize double crop** on the better ground. This is the backbone — it feeds us and brings in steady cash.
- **2 mu cotton** on the western plot. I used to grow more cotton, but picking cotton at my age is brutal. I keep 2 mu because the price has been decent and I can still manage it with my wife plus hired help for the picking.

**Winter wheat (6 mu, already planted mid-October):**
I put down about 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu before planting, with 18 kg of seed — I use Jimai 22, same variety as most of my neighbors, reliable on this soil. Right now the wheat is at jointing, so next week I'll topdress around 12 kg urea per mu together with the spring irrigation. That's my one big nitrogen push. I'll probably irrigate two more times — jointing now, then grain filling in May. The well is metered and pumping is expensive, so three irrigations total is my limit unless it's a real dry spring. I'll spray for weeds in the next few days and watch for powdery mildew and rust as it warms up. Expecting around 470 kg/mu — last year I got 485, the year before 450. It depends on the May weather.

**Summer maize (6 mu, plant mid-June right after wheat):**
The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is tight — less than a week. I hire the combine for wheat and the no-till planter comes right behind. Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605, hybrid seed about 4 kg/mu, I pay around 30 yuan/kg. I side-dress 40 kg compound at planting and then about 15 kg urea at V8-V10 when the plants are knee-high. Total N around 17 kg/mu. Maize rarely needs irrigation here if the summer rains come — but if July is dry at tasseling, I'll irrigate once. That's the critical stage. One spray for corn borer in late July. Expecting 520 kg/mu.

**Cotton (2 mu, planting now in late April):**
I cover with plastic film — it helps with soil temperature and saves one irrigation. Bt hybrid seed, about 2 kg/mu, around 80 yuan/kg. Cotton is hungry — I put 50 kg compound per mu before planting and then topdress 20 kg urea plus some potash at budding and again lightly at flowering. Pesticide is the big expense: even with Bt I spray 4-5 times for aphids, whitefly, and bollworm spillover. Picking is the hard part — three picks from September through October. My wife and I do the first pick, then I hire two neighbors for about 10 days for the second and third. Expecting 260 kg/mu lint.

**What I'm worried about this year:**
Fertilizer prices are still high. Pumping costs keep rising. And honestly, at 76 I'm watching how much I commit to — I don't want to get halfway through and have to hire expensive labor because my back gives out. So I'm sticking to what I know works. No new varieties, no fancy changes. Maybe my last few years running this place on my own.
